detail.divText: Don’t judge it by salary alone; compare the work, cost of living, people you’d leave behind, and whether the new city opens a door you actually want to walk through. Imagine an ordinary Tuesday there—not the shiny first week—and notice whether that life feels larger or merely busier. What would you regret more in a year: taking it, or letting it pass?

Don’t decide on salary alone; take it if the role gives you better skills, autonomy, and a life you can actually afford after rent and relocation. A shiny finish cannot rescue weak joinery, lah. What would this move give you that your current job cannot?

Don’t judge the offer by salary alone; compare growth, cost of living, daily routine, support network, and how reversible the move would be if it doesn’t suit you. I’d take it if it moves you toward the life you want—not merely away from a job you dislike. Which part of the offer feels exciting, and which part is making you hesitate?

Take it only if it improves your long-term trajectory, not merely your salary; relocation can make a shiny offer expensive very quickly. What would you gain there that your current job cannot realistically give you?

Don’t judge it by salary alone—compare growth, cost of living, work culture, and what the move gives your life outside the office. If it still feels like an upgrade after subtracting relocation costs and disruption, I’d lean yes. Which part is making you hesitate most: the job itself or leaving your current city?
